messages:
Amy K: quick sync — we need to pick a path for cohort-based routing + compact trace envelopes before the next ingest cutover. two options on the table: 1) tag cohorts at edge and route to cohort-specific shards, 2) route to shared shard and do cohorting downstream. pros/cons attached in thread.
Rahul S: tl;dr preference?
Amy K: lean toward edge cohort tagging because it preserves cost attribution and avoids late backfills, but worried about header size and sdk churn.
Olivia P: +1 on attribution. can we use a tiny cohort id (8 bytes) instead of full billing key to keep headers small?
Jordan M: we discussed that in the gating RFC — small id mapping table at ingest can map cohort id -> billing attributes. concern: extra lookup on ingest adds latency.
Amy K: real numbers: current p50 ingest path is ~12ms. extra lookup if cached hit is ~1.5ms, miss is ~20ms (db). caching hit rate likely >95% for common tenants.
Rahul S: what about namespace collision and rollout complexity? if SDK starts adding cohort-id header we need versioning and backward compat.
Olivia P: rollout plan idea: SDK adds header only when configured by env; edge proxy sets header for supported clients during canary; fallback is ‘cohort-unknown’ and we route to shared shard. low-risk.
Jordan M: operationally, how do we handle sampling/kv-cache interplay? cohort-specific shards might see skewed sequence length distributions — could impact kernel-selection heuristics.
Amy K: true — suggestion: allow per-cohort runtime profile overrides (max_seq, batch_size) but default to global. that lets big-batch cohorts scale separately.
Rahul S: security note — cohort id -> billing attrs mapping must be validated server-side and not trusted from client. treat header as hint only, verify against auth context.
Olivia P: agreed. also prefer compact wire format: header name `x-rw-cohort` value base62 encoded. example: `x-rw-cohort: q1b9zA`
Amy K: quick example of minimal envelope we discussed:
```
{ "cohort": "q1b9zA", "trace_id": "...", "spans": [...] }
```
Jordan M: k. can we do an A/B test? cohort-routing enabled for 10% traffic, 1k tenants in cohort mapping table, measure latency + cost delta + attribution correctness.
Rahul S: +1. metrics to track: ingest-p50/95/99, mapping-cache-hit-rate, billing-join-failures, query-latency for cohort-sharded queries, token-cost-per-req.
Amy K: ops playbook: if mapping-db latency spikes -> switch header-to-shared-shard fallback, auto-roll disable via feature flag. deploy-bot: can you create feature flag and 10% rollout?
deploy-bot: created flag `cohort_routing_canary` targeting 10% of traffic. rollout id: ff-2026-03-21-001.
Olivia P: timeline suggestion: implement SDK header + edge proxy support this sprint, ingest verification + mapping service next, canary the week after.
Jordan M: action items: 1) Rahul: sketch mapping table schema + TTLs, 2) Amy: write ingest verification checks + fallback logic, 3) Olivia: SDK + proxy stubs, 4) me: perf test harness for shard skew.
Rahul S: I'll post schema in #eng-platform later today.
Amy K: thanks team — this feels like the lowest-risk path that preserves attribution and keeps ability to fall back. we'll reconvene after perf results. :thumbsup:
